text: One of the things after you've been in engineering for a while is that develop this tendency to immediately respond with no to new ideas.
speaker: Vijay Iyengar
context: Lenny asks Vijay what he had to unlearn as an engineer when transitioning to product leadership. Vijay explains how engineers develop a defensive mindset against new ideas because they experience the ongoing maintenance burden of poorly thought-out features. This creates what he calls 'scar tissue' - a protective response that makes engineers reflexively reject new proposals with a 'hard no' to avoid future problems.
text_ko: 엔지니어로 오래 일하다 보면 새 아이디어에 대해 일단 거절부터 하는 버릇이 생겨요.
text_zh: 在工程岗位待久了，会有个毛病：对新想法下意识就先说「不」。
text_es: Después de un tiempo en ingeniería, tiendes a responder automáticamente "no" a las ideas nuevas.
key_sentence: develop this tendency to immediately respond with no to new ideas.
original_text: One of the things after you've been in engineering for a while is that develop this tendency to immediately respond with no to new ideas. And I think from the engineering perspective, this is because you spend a lot of your time building and maintaining ideas that maybe are half thought out or didn't really go anywhere, and you just feel like the full brunt of the maintenance cost of that. And so you build up the scar tissue and this immune response to say no to new ideas, and it's a hard no, like no, we're definitely not going to do it.

vocabulary.definition: A tendency is an inclination or a habitual pattern of behavior or thought that is often observed over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, recognizing tendencies can help leaders anticipate employee reactions, market trends, or consumer behavior, which is crucial for strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'tendency' often implies a natural inclination, it can also suggest a lack of critical thinking or openness to change when used in a negative context.

vocabulary.definition: To respond means to react or reply to a stimulus, question, or situation in a timely manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, effective response mechanisms are essential for customer service, crisis management, and team collaboration, ensuring that issues are addressed promptly.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply varying degrees of engagement, from a simple acknowledgment to a detailed and thoughtful reply, depending on the context.

text: The issue for us at the time was that we took people away from the investment in our core product to go do those other things. We moved people, right?
speaker: Vijay Iyengar
context: Lenny asks about Mixpanel's journey of expanding to multiple products and then refocusing back to their core analytics product. Vijay explains the strategic mistake they made - they moved engineering resources away from their core product to build adjacent products, which made them vulnerable to competitors who could outinvest them in analytics. His key insight is that market leaders should maintain their investment advantage in their core product while funding new ventures with profits, not people.
text_ko: 그때 우리의 문제는 핵심 제품(core product)에 대한 투자에서 인력을 빼서 다른 일에 투입했다는 거예요. 사람들을 옮겼잖아요?
text_zh: 当时的问题是，我们把人从核心产品(core product)的投入上抽走，去做那些别的事。我们确实把人挪走了，对吧？
text_es: El problema para nosotros en ese momento era que estábamos sacando personal de la inversión en nuestro producto principal (core product) para que trabajara en esas otras cosas. Movimos a gente, ¿no?
key_sentence: We took people away from the investment in our core product to go do those other things.
original_text: The issue for us at the time was that we took people away from the investment in our core product to go do those other things. We moved people, right? And so the trap there is that you leave yourself ripe for disruption in your core because someone else can out invest you in that core. And so if you are the leader in some core product, our takeaway here is you should continue to out invest everyone else in that core and then invest the profits that come out of that core into the next venture.

vocabulary.definition: The primary offering of a company that is central to its business model and value proposition. It represents the main source of revenue and customer interest.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, the core product is often the focus of development and marketing efforts, as it is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage and customer loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'core product' emphasizes the essential nature of the offering, it is important to differentiate it from ancillary products or services that may support the core but are not central to the business.

vocabulary.definition: The allocation of resources, typically financial, with the expectation of generating a return or profit over time. It can also refer to time or effort spent on a project.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and business contexts, investment is crucial for funding operations, scaling growth, and developing new products or services.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'investment' can imply a long-term commitment, and it is often associated with risk; thus, it is important to assess potential returns carefully.

text: But one of the traps with RICE that we observed is that the C and E, the confidence and effort tends to cause you to prematurely deprioritize potentially high reach, high impact bets, really innovative things.
speaker: Vijay Iyengar
context: Lenny asks about prioritization frameworks and Vijay's approach to helping product teams prioritize effectively. Vijay discusses the RICE framework (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) and explains a common pitfall - the Confidence and Effort components often cause teams to unfairly penalize innovative, high-impact ideas because these factors are inherently unclear for breakthrough concepts. He describes how his team experienced this when they applied RICE and all the most innovative ideas scored poorly.
text_ko: 저희가 RICE(Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort)를 보며 관찰한 함정 중 하나는 C와 E, 즉 확신(confidence)과 노력(effort)이 잠재적으로 도달 범위(Reach)와 영향(Impact)이 큰, 정말 혁신적인 시도들의 우선순위를 성급하게 낮추게 만든다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 我们发现 RICE 框架（RICE）有个陷阱：C 和 E，即置信度(confidence)和投入(effort)，常常会让你过早把那些可能覆盖面广、影响力大、真正有创新性的大胆押注降到次要位置。
text_es: Una de las trampas del método RICE (RICE) que hemos observado es que la C y la E, la confianza (confidence) y el esfuerzo (effort), suelen llevarte a dejar en segundo plano demasiado pronto apuestas con potencial de gran alcance y alto impacto, cosas realmente innovadoras.
key_sentence: RICE can prematurely deprioritize high reach, high impact bets due to murky confidence.
original_text: But one of the traps with RICE that we observed is that the C and E, the confidence and effort tends to cause you to prematurely deprioritize potentially high reach, high impact bets, really innovative things. And we encountered this on one of our teams early last year were we just RICE'd everything, all the ideas, and a lot of the high reach, high impact things ended up at the bottom because confidence and effort were just so murky for them, as they should be typically for high reach, high impact ideas.

vocabulary.definition: To assign a lower priority to something, often resulting in reduced focus or resources allocated to it.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, deprioritizing can occur when teams shift their focus away from certain projects or initiatives in favor of others deemed more critical to immediate goals.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that something valuable may be overlooked or undervalued.

vocabulary.definition: Having the capacity to develop into something in the future; possible but not yet actualized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'potentially' is frequently used to describe opportunities, risks, or outcomes that could arise based on current trends or decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While it indicates possibility, it does not guarantee success, so it should be used cautiously to avoid overpromising.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by the introduction of new ideas, methods, or products; creative and forward-thinking.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, being innovative is crucial for staying competitive and meeting evolving consumer demands.
vocabulary.nuance: This term is often associated with positive change and progress, but it can imply risk if the innovation is untested or radical.

text: you make the time box or an appetite the input, and you say, 'We want to solve X problem and we're willing to invest six weeks solving that problem.
speaker: Vijay Iyengar
context: Lenny and Vijay are discussing estimation challenges in product development. Vijay explains the core problem with traditional estimation - teams are asked to estimate before they fully understand what they're building. He introduces the 'appetite over estimates' concept from Basecamp's Shape Up methodology, where instead of estimating how long something will take, you decide upfront how much time you're willing to invest in solving a particular problem.
text_ko: 타임박스(time box)나 투자 여력(appetite)을 입력값으로 삼고, “우리는 X 문제를 해결하려고 하고 그걸 해결하는 데 6주를 투자할 의향이 있다”라고 말하는 거예요.
text_zh: 你把时间限定(time box)或投入意愿(appetite)当作输入，然后就说：‘我们要解决X问题，愿意投入六周时间来解决它。’
text_es: Pones como insumo (input) un límite de tiempo (time box) o un apetito (appetite) y dices: "Queremos resolver el problema X y estamos dispuestos a dedicar seis semanas a resolverlo."
key_sentence: We want to solve X problem and we're willing to invest six weeks solving that problem.
original_text: One approach that I found really interesting is from this book called Shape Up by Basecamp, which this idea of appetite over estimates, where instead of making the estimate an output of planning, you make the time box or an appetite the input, and you say, 'We want to solve X problem and we're willing to invest six weeks solving that problem.'

text: And one of the rituals that it's enabled is we'll find that engineers will go into that channel and react with a message with an email emoji, which means I'm going to email this customer and find out more, right?
speaker: Vijay Iyengar
context: Lenny asks about Mixpanel's unique approach to keeping product teams close to customers. Vijay explains how they created an automated Slack feed of customer feedback that all engineers and designers can access directly. He describes a ritual that emerged where engineers use emoji reactions to signal they'll reach out to customers directly, then email them to dig deeper into problems using techniques like the 'five whys' to understand root causes and improve the product independently.
text_ko: 그리고 그걸 가능하게 한 관행 중 하나는 엔지니어들이 그 채널(channel)에 들어가 이메일 이모지(email emoji)로 반응하면서 '이 고객에게 이메일 보내서 더 알아볼게요'라고 메시지를 남기는 걸 보는 거예요.
text_zh: 它促成的一个惯例是，我们会看到工程师进到那个频道 (channel)，在消息上点一个邮件表情 (email emoji)，意思就是“我要给这个客户发封邮件再问清楚”，对吧？
text_es: Uno de los rituales que ha generado es que vemos a los ingenieros entrar en ese canal y poner un emoji de correo (email emoji) en el mensaje, lo que viene a decir: "voy a enviarle un correo electrónico (email) a este cliente para averiguar más", ¿no?
key_sentence: engineers will go into that channel and react with a message with an email emoji, which means I'm going to email this customer
original_text: And one of the rituals that it's enabled is we'll find that engineers will go into that channel and react with a message with an email emoji, which means I'm going to email this customer and find out more, right? And they'll just email the customer and say, 'Hey, I'm the engineer that built this feature. I saw you said this specific thing. Can you tell me more? I'd love to understand.' They ask the five why's, and then they improve the product on their own.

vocabulary.definition: To respond to a stimulus or situation, often with an action or message.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, 'react' often refers to how team members respond to communications or events, such as customer inquiries or internal discussions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'react' implies a spontaneous response, it can also suggest a need for quick decision-making in fast-paced settings.

vocabulary.definition: Professionals who apply scientific and mathematical principles to design, develop, and maintain structures, systems, or products.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology companies, engineers are pivotal in product development, ensuring that solutions are both functional and innovative.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'engineers' often connotes technical expertise, and it can imply a collaborative role within interdisciplinary teams.

text: I think the biggest mistake is setting up analytics using client side SDKs, client side tracking. So, web and mobile SDKs, putting a mixpanel.track or segment.track in your web app or your mobile apps.
speaker: Vijay Iyengar
context: Lenny asks Vijay what most people get wrong when setting up product analytics, given his expertise as head of product at Mixpanel. Vijay shares what he calls a 'hot take' - that using client-side SDKs for tracking is a major mistake. He explains that many people assume product analytics requires putting tracking code directly in web and mobile apps, but this approach consistently leads to poor data quality and maintenance challenges, contradicting common industry practice.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 가장 큰 실수는 애널리틱스(analytics)를 클라이언트 측 SDK(client-side SDKs), 클라이언트 측 트래킹(client-side tracking)으로 구축하는 거예요. 즉 웹(Web)과 모바일(Mobile) SDK를 써서 웹 앱이나 모바일 앱에 mixpanel.track이나 segment.track 같은 트래킹 호출을 직접 넣는 거죠.
text_zh: 我觉得最大的错误是把数据分析（analytics）放在客户端，用客户端 SDK（client-side SDKs）来做客户端埋点（client-side tracking）。也就是在网页和移动端的 SDK（web and mobile SDKs）里，直接把 mixpanel.track 或 segment.track 放到你的网页应用（web app）或移动应用（mobile apps）里。
text_es: Creo que el mayor error es montar la analítica usando kits de desarrollo (SDKs) del lado del cliente, es decir, hacer el seguimiento (tracking) en el cliente. Por ejemplo, poner un mixpanel.track o un segment.track en tu aplicación web o móvil.
key_sentence: I think the biggest mistake is setting up analytics using client side SDKs, client side tracking.
original_text: I think the biggest mistake is setting up analytics using client side SDKs, client side tracking. So, web and mobile SDKs, putting a mixpanel.track or segment.track in your web app or your mobile apps. And reason it's a hot take is that for many people that's product analytics and SDK tracking are synonymous. They're like, 'All right, Mixpanel means SDK, I have to put an SDK in my web and mobile app. But that's a mistake because it... We've just seen time and time again, it leads to poor data quality and difficulty to maintain that data.

vocabulary.definition: Analytics refers to the systematic computational analysis of data or statistics, often used to gain insights and inform decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, analytics is crucial for understanding customer behavior, measuring performance, and optimizing strategies based on data-driven insights.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with quantitative data, analytics can also encompass qualitative insights, making it important to choose the right type for the context.

vocabulary.definition: Tracking involves monitoring and recording user interactions or behaviors over time, often through various digital tools and technologies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and product development, tracking is vital for understanding user engagement, measuring campaign effectiveness, and improving product features based on user feedback.
vocabulary.nuance: Tracking can raise privacy concerns, so it is important to balance data collection with ethical considerations and user consent.
